title.en: The Ascension from the Mount of Olives

texts.period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 1

summary.en: Forty days of risen appearances end as 'he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.' Two men in white apparel ask the gazing disciples, 'why stand ye gazing up into heaven? this same Jesus... shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven' — and the company returns to Jerusalem to pray in the upper room, one hundred and twenty strong, awaiting the promise of the Spirit.
summary.zh: 四十日復活顯現終結之時，「他就被取上升，有一朵雲彩把他接去」。兩個白衣人問呆望天空的門徒：「加利利人哪，你們為甚麼站著望天呢？這離開你們被接升天的耶穌……他怎樣往天上去，你們還要怎樣來。」眾人回耶路撒冷，在樓上房間同心合意恆切禱告——一百二十人等候聖靈的應許。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The ascension is celebrated as a principal feast; the return-promise frames Christian eschatology.

passages.text: And when he had spoken these things, while they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight. And while they looked stedfastly toward heaven as he went up, behold, two men stood by them in white apparel; which also said, Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven? this same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.

Then returned they unto Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is from Jerusalem a sabbath day's journey. And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes. These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brethren.

title.en: Ananias and Sapphira Lie to the Holy Ghost
title.zh: 亞拿尼亞與撒非喇欺哄聖靈

texts.period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 5

summary.en: In the community where 'neither said any of them that ought of the things which he possessed was his own', Ananias and Sapphira sell land, keep back part of the price, and present the rest as the whole. Peter's rebuke — 'thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God' — is followed by sudden death, his, then three hours later hers at the same feet; 'great fear came upon all the church.' The young church's feared and debated tale of concealed giving.
summary.zh: 在「沒有一人說他的東西有一樣是自己的」的團體中，亞拿尼亞夫婦賣田產，私自留下幾分，其餘放在使徒腳前充作全數。彼得斥責——「你不是欺哄人，是欺哄神了」——隨即仆倒斷氣；三小時後妻子在同樣腳前同樣倒下。「全教會和聽見這事的人都甚懼怕。」初期教會最令人戰慄、也最被爭論的隱匿奉獻故事。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The deaths are presented as narrative without endorsement.

passages.text: But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession, and kept back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it, and brought a certain part, and laid it at the apostles' feet. But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost, and to keep back part of the price of the land? Whiles it remained, was it not thine own? and after it was sold, was it not in thine own power? why hast thou conceived this thing in thine heart? thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God. And Ananias hearing these words fell down, and gave up the ghost: and great fear came on all them that heard these things.

And it was about the space of three hours after, when his wife, not knowing what was done, came in. And Peter answered unto her, Tell me whether ye sold the land for so much? And she said, Yea, for so much. Then Peter said unto her, How is it that ye have agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Lord? behold, the feet of them which have buried thy husband are at the door, and shall carry thee out. Then fell she down straightway at his feet, and yielded up the ghost: and great fear came upon all the church.

title.en: The Stoning of Stephen, First Martyr
title.zh: 首位殉道者司提反被石頭打死

texts.period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapters 6-7

summary.en: Full of the Holy Ghost, Stephen sees 'the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God'; the council stops their ears, casts him out, and stones him — with the clothes laid at the feet of the young man Saul, consenting. Stephen's last words fold the tradition's martyrdom pattern: 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit... Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep.' The persecution scatters the church, and the gospel spreads.
summary.zh: 滿得聖靈的司提反舉目望天，見「天開了，人子站在神的右邊」；公會捂耳呼喊，把他推到城外用石頭打——見證人把衣裳放在旁邊的少年人掃羅腳前。司提反臨終呼求確立殉道模式：「求主耶穌接收我的靈魂……主啊，不要將這罪歸於他們。說了這話，就睡了。」教會遭大逼迫四散，福音反得廣傳。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The prototype martyr; the Saul connection is the hinge of the Damascus conversion.

passages.text: When they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed on him with their teeth. But he, being full of the Holy Ghost, looked up stedfastly into heaven, and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God, and said, Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God.

Then they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears, and ran upon him with one accord, and cast him out of the city, and stoned him: and the witnesses laid down their clothes at a young man's feet, whose name was Saul. And they stoned Stephen, calling upon God, and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep. And Saul was consenting unto his death. And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judaea and Samaria.

region.en: Desert road from Jerusalem to Gaza
region.zh: 耶路撒冷下迦薩的路上

texts.period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 8

summary.en: Sent by an angel onto the desert road, Philip catches the treasurer of Candace, queen of Ethiopia, reading Isaiah in his chariot — 'Understandest thou what thou readest?... How can I, except some man should guide me?' Philip preaches Jesus from the suffering servant passage; at the water by the road the eunuch asks, 'what doth hinder me to be baptized?' — and is baptized, going on his way rejoicing, while Philip is caught away by the Spirit. African Christianity has long claimed this as its founding charter.
summary.zh: 使者差腓利上那條通往迦薩的曠野路，追上埃提阿伯女王干大基手下總管銀庫的太監——他正坐在車上誦讀以賽亞書。「你所念的，你明白嗎？……沒有人指教我，怎能明白呢？」腓利便從受苦僕人的經文傳講耶穌；路旁有水，太監問「我受洗有甚麼妨礙呢？」——受洗後歡歡喜喜走路，腓利被主的靈提了去。非洲教會久以本章為建基憲章。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The Ethiopian eunuch is honored in Ethiopian Orthodox memory as the bearer of the faith.

passages.text: And the angel of the Lord spake unto Philip, saying, Arise, and go toward the south unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza, which is desert. And he arose and went: and, behold, a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who had the charge of all her treasure, and had come to Jerusalem for to worship, was returning, and sitting in his chariot read Esaias the prophet. Then the Spirit said unto Philip, Go near, and join thyself to this chariot. And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest? And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me?

Then Philip opened his mouth, and began at the same scripture, and preached unto him Jesus. And as they went on their way, they came unto a certain water: and the eunuch said, See, here is water; what doth hinder me to be baptized? And Philip said, If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest. And he answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God. And he commanded the chariot to stand still: and they went down both into the water, both Philip and the eunuch; and he baptized him. And when they were come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more: and he went on his way rejoicing.

title.en: Saul on the Road to Damascus

texts.period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 9

summary.en: Breathing threatenings and slaughter, the persecutor travels to Damascus with warrants for 'this way'; suddenly a light from heaven shines around him and he falls to earth: 'Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?... I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.' Led blind into the city, he is met three days later by the disciple Ananias — 'a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles' — receives his sight like scales falling, is baptized, and straightway preaches Christ in the synagogues.
summary.zh: 口吐威嚇兇殺話的逼迫者，持大祭司公文往大馬士革捉拿「信奉這道的人」；忽然天上有大光四面照著他，他就仆倒在地：「掃羅，掃羅，你為甚麼逼迫我？……我就是你所逼迫的耶穌。你用腳踢刺是難的。」被拉進城，三日看不見、不吃不喝；門徒亞拿尼亞奉命去按手——「他是我所揀選的器皿，要在外邦人和君王並以色列人面前宣揚我的名」——鱗狀的東西掉下，他就看見，起來受洗，隨即在各會堂宣講耶穌。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The conversion is the hinge of Christian universalism; tagged theophany for the heavenly light and voice.

passages.text: And Saul, yet breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went unto the high priest, and desired of him letters to Damascus to the synagogues, that if he found any of this way, whether they were men or women, he might bring them bound unto Jerusalem. And as he journeyed, he came near Damascus: and suddenly there shined round about him a light from heaven: and he fell to the earth, and heard a voice saying unto him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.

And Saul arose from the earth; and when his eyes were opened, he saw no man: but they led him by the hand, and brought him into Damascus. And he was three days without sight, and neither did eat nor drink. And there was a certain disciple at Damascus, named Ananias; and to him said the Lord in a vision, Ananias. And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the street which is called Straight, and enquire in the house of Judas for one called Saul, of Tarsus: for, behold, he prayeth.

But the Lord said unto him, Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel: for I will shew him how great things he must suffer for my name's sake. And Ananias went his way, and entered into the house; and putting his hands on him said, Brother Saul, the Lord, even Jesus, that appeared unto thee in the way as thou camest, hath sent me, that thou mightest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Ghost. And immediately there fell from his eyes as it had been scales: and he received sight forthwith, and arose, and was baptized.

title.en: Peter's Sheet Vision and Cornelius's Household
title.zh: 彼得的布異象與哥尼流一家

texts.period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 10

summary.en: Praying hungry on a rooftop, Peter falls into a trance: heaven opens, a great sheet knitted at four corners descends full of unclean beasts, and a voice commands, 'Rise, Peter; kill, and eat' — 'What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common', thrice repeated. Sent for by Cornelius, the God-fearing centurion, Peter preaches in Caesarea and the Holy Ghost falls on the uncircumcised hearers — 'Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we?' The charter of the Gentile mission.
summary.zh: 屋頂禱告時餓了的彼得魂遊象外：天開了，四角垂下的大布縑滿俗物與不潔之物，聲音說「彼得，起來，宰了吃」——「神所潔淨的，你不可當作俗物」，一連三次。羅馬百夫長哥尼流遣人相請；彼得在該撒利亞講道，聖靈降在一切未受割禮的聽道者身上——「這些人既受了聖靈，與我們一樣，誰能禁止用水給他們施洗呢？」外邦宣教的憲章自此立定。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The sheet vision is the tradition's charter of universality and the overturning of purity codes.

passages.text: Peter went up upon the housetop to pray about the sixth hour: and he became very hungry, and would have eaten: but while they made ready, he fell into a trance, and saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending upon him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners, and let down to the earth: wherein were all manner of fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air. And there came a voice to him, Rise, Peter; kill, and eat. But Peter said, Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean. And the voice spake unto him again the second time, What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common. This was done thrice: and the vessel was received up again into heaven.

While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word. And they of the circumcision which believed were astonished, as many as came with Peter, because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost: for they heard them speak with tongues, and magnify God. Then answered Peter, Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we? And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord.

title.en: The Angel Breaks Peter Out of Prison

texts.period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 12

summary.en: Intending to bring Peter forth after Passover, Herod keeps him sleeping bound with two chains between soldiers — while the church prays without ceasing. The angel smites Peter on the side, the chains fall off, the iron gate 'opened to them of his own accord'; Peter thinks it a vision until the angel departs and he stands alone in the street — 'Now I know of a surety, that the LORD hath sent his angel' — and comes to Mary's house where the praying church can hardly believe the knocking is really him.
summary.zh: 希律要在逾越節後提彼得出來辦他，彼得卻被兩條鐵鏈鎖著睡在二兵士之間——教會卻為他切切禱告神。使者拍他的肋旁，鐵鏈脫落；「臨街的鐵門就自己開了」；他以為見異象，直到天使離開，才獨立街中——「我現在真知道主差遣他的使者，救我脫離希律的手」——到了馬利亞家門口，禱告的人群竟不敢相信真是他敲門。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The prison-delivery is a classic angelic-rescue type.

passages.text: Peter therefore was kept in prison: but prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for him. And when Herod would have brought him forth, the same night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains: and the keepers before the door kept the prison. And, behold, the angel of the Lord came upon him, and a light shined in the prison: and he smote Peter on the side, and raised him up, saying, Arise up quickly. And his chains fell off from his hands.

When they were past the first and the second ward, they came unto the iron gate that leadeth unto the city; which opened to them of his own accord: and they went out, and passed on through one street; and forthwith the angel departed from him. And when Peter was come to himself, he said, Now I know of a surety, that the LORD hath sent his angel, and hath delivered me out of the hand of Herod. And when he had considered the thing, he came to the house of Mary the mother of John, whose surname was Mark; where many were gathered together praying.

title.en: Midnight Hymns in the Philippian Jail
title.zh: 腓立比監中的半夜歌聲

texts.period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 16

summary.en: Answering a night vision — 'a man of Macedonia... Come over into Macedonia, and help us' — Paul crosses to Europe, converts the purple-seller Lydia, and after an exorcism is beaten and jailed with Silas. At midnight they pray and sing; an earthquake opens every door and looses every band; the suicide-minded jailer is stopped — 'Do thyself no harm: for we are all here' — asks 'what must I do to be saved?', washes their stripes, and is baptized with all his house the same hour of the night.
summary.zh: 應夜間異象——「有一個馬其頓人站著求他說：請你過到馬其頓來幫助我們」——保羅渡海入歐洲，使賣紫色布疋的呂底亞歸主；因趕鬼被棍打下監。半夜與西拉禱告唱詩，大地震動，眾門全開、鎖鏈鬆開；欲自刎的禁卒被喝止——「不要傷害自己，我們都在這裏」——問「我當怎樣行才可以得救？」當夜洗淨他們的傷，全家立時受洗。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The Macedonian call is the charter of the gospel's entry into Europe.

passages.text: And a vision appeared to Paul in the night; There stood a man of Macedonia, and prayed him, saying, Come over into Macedonia, and help us. And after he had seen the vision, immediately we endeavoured to go into Macedonia, assuredly gathering that the Lord had called us for to preach the gospel unto them. And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God, heard us: whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul. And when she was baptized, and her household, she besought us, saying, If ye have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house, and abide there.

And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them. And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one's bands were loosed. And the keeper of the prison awaking out of his sleep, and seeing the prison doors open, he drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had been fled. But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm: for we are all here.

Then he called for a light, and sprang in, and came trembling, and fell down before Paul and Silas, and brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved? And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house. And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, straightway. And when he had brought them into his house, he set meat before them, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house.

title.en: Paul at the Areopagus: The Unknown God
title.zh: 保羅在亞略巴古：未識之神

texts.period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 17

summary.en: In the city wholly given to idolatry, philosophers of the Epicureans and Stoicks summon the 'babbler' to Mars' hill, 'for all the Athenians... spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell, or to hear some new thing.' Paul's address builds on their own altar: 'TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you' — God who made the world dwells not in temples made with hands, has 'determined the times before appointed', and 'now commandeth all men every where to repent', guaranteeing judgment 'by that man whom he hath ordained.'
summary.zh: 在滿城偶像的雅典，伊壁鳩魯與斯多亞學士把這「胡言亂語的」帶到亞略巴古——「雅典人和住在那裏的客人都不顧別的事，只或談說，或聽聽新聞」。保羅的講章由他們自己的祭壇起筵：「未識之神。你們所不認識而敬拜的，我現在告訴你們」——創造天地的神不住人手所造的殿，已預定時期，「如今卻吩咐各處的人都要悔改」，並藉祂所立定的人按公義審判天下。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The Areopagus speech is the classic model of cross-cultural apologetics.

passages.text: Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry. Then certain philosophers of the Epicureans, and of the Stoicks, encountered him. And some said, What will this babbler say? other some, He seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods: because he preached unto them Jesus, and the resurrection. And they took him, and brought him unto Areopagus, saying, May we know what this new doctrine, whereof thou speakest, is?

Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars' hill, and said, Ye men of Athens, I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious. For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you. God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands; neither is worshipped with men's hands, as though he needed any thing.

title.en: Shipwreck at Malta: The Viper and the Gods
title.zh: 馬耳他海難：毒蛇與「他是神」

texts.period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapters 27-28

summary.en: Fourteen days tossed by the Euroclydon with neither sun nor stars, all hope gone, Paul stands amid the crew and announces his night-visiting angel: 'Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.' The ship runs aground; soldiers spare the prisoners; all swim or float ashore at Melita, where a viper fastens on Paul's hand — 'No doubt this man is a murderer' — and he shakes it off unharmed, so that the islanders change their verdict to 'he was a god', and Publius's father is healed.
summary.zh: 被「友拉革羅」狂風拋蕩十四日，不見日頭星辰，得救的指望都絕了——保羅卻在眾人中宣告夜間天使的話：「保羅，不要害怕，你必定站在該撒面前；並且與你同船的人，神都賜給你了。」船擱淺，兵士保全囚犯；全船二百七十六人或游或浮抵岸。保羅拾柴生火，毒蛇咬住其手——「這人必是個兇手」——他竟甩進火裏毫無損傷，島人改口說他是神；部百流的父親亦蒙醫治。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The sea-voyage is the most detailed itinerary in Acts; the viper scene is a classic sign.

passages.text: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon. And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive. And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship; and the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship. And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away. But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me. And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man's life among you, but of the ship. For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve, saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.

And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore. And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves. And the soldiers' counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape. But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and they escaped all safe to land.

And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita. And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand. And when the barbarians saw the venomous beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he hath escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffereth not to live. And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm. Howbeit they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.

title.en: Eutychus Falls from the Third Loft
title.zh: 猶推古從三樓窗戶墜落

texts.period: Acts of the Apostles, c. 80-90 CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 44: Acts, chapter 20

summary.en: The church meets on the first day of the week to break bread, 'ready to depart on the morrow; and he continued his speech until midnight' — and in the lamplit window sits the youth Eutychus, who 'sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third loft, and was taken up dead.' Paul goes down, embraces him, and his life is restored; the breaking of bread resumes till daybreak, 'and they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted.'
summary.zh: 七日的頭一日聚會擘餅——「保羅因為要次日起行，就講論直到半夜」——燭光中坐在窗臺的少年猶推古沉睡墜樓，「扶他起來，已經死了」。保羅下去伏在他身上抱著說「不要發慌，他的靈魂還在」；隨後回到樓上擘餅直到天亮——「有人把那童子活活的領來，他們得安慰不小。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The first-day breaking-of-bread meeting is cited for the early Lord's-day practice.

passages.text: And upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the morrow; and continued his speech until midnight. And there were many lights in the upper chamber, where they were gathered together. And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third loft, and was taken up dead.

And Paul went down, and fell on him, and embracing him said, Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him. When he therefore was come up again, and had broken bread, and eaten, and talked a long while, even till break of day, so he departed. And they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted.
